audit.whatIsWrong: The content layer says the outer half of Tactical Sweep (W) deals true damage, in the level 3-5 spike, the early text and whys[2]-[3]. True damage is on Precision Protocol (Q), not on Tactical Sweep. Adaptive Defenses (P) is never mentioned at all.
audit.why: Riot's Tactical Sweep text: 'Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille' — extra damage and a heal, no true damage. The kit's trueDamage flag sits on Precision Protocol, whose text is the delayed-recast empowered attack. Pointing the player at the wrong source changes what they build: the answer to Tactical Sweep is Grievous Wounds, and the answer to Precision Protocol is not resistances at all. Adaptive Defenses shields Camille off basic attacks against the damage type she is being hit by, so Cassiopeia's unprimed magic chip literally funds a magic shield.
audit.corrected: Tactical Sweep described as bonus damage plus heal, true damage moved to Precision Protocol, Adaptive Defenses and anti-heal added.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart hands Cassiopeia Level 3, Level 6 and two-item while the prose says the opposite for the first two, and marks Levels 4-5 and First item as Skill when the prose calls them hers outright.
audit.why: spikes[1] is titled her kill window at Lvl 3-5; the mid text opens 'Levels 4-6 are hers'; whys[4] says The Hextech Ultimatum collapses the whole Cassiopeia pattern; whys[5] says 'the lane stays hers' through first item. Only Level 1 and the grouped two-item stage are Cassiopeia's, and whys[1] describes Level 2 as neither side committing.
audit.corrected: win[1]=Skill, win[2..5]=Camille, with the full-layer phase sides matched.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot is named as the clock the lane runs on in six places and its cooldown appears in none of them.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12s and The Hextech Ultimatum is 140/115/90s. Sixteen seconds is a long window for a champion who casts Noxious Blast every 3.5s and Twin Fang every 0.75s — that is the concrete shape of when to step up, and it was never stated.
audit.corrected: Hookshot's 16s and the Ultimatum's 140s now appear in the win condition, cooldown block, do's, mid text and all-in windows.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 are hers. Extra ranks in Tactical Sweep (W) mean its true-damage outer edge plus the empowered Q can chunk me past where my E-spam recovers, and at 6 her Hextech Ultimatum (R) is the nightmare — the barrier seals me into a 1v1 and walls off the minions my poison pattern feeds on, and my Petrifying Gaze (R) only catches her if she's facing me inside the box. I throw Miasma (W) on her dash path to ground the Hookshot, but if her E is up and my W is down she picks the fight. Survive this stretch: farm under tower, sidestep the wall stun, and bait out her E before I ever commit.

notes: Two _missing-interactions rules for this matchup are unsupported by Riot's text and I did not act on either. 'Camille's The Hextech Ultimatum (R) is a channel — your Petrifying Gaze (R) cancels it outright' and 'Camille can go untargetable through your commit (The Hextech Ultimatum)' both come from channel/untargetable flags on her R, but Riot's description is only 'Camille dashes to target champion, anchoring them to the area. She also deals bonus magic damage to the target with her basic attacks' — no channel, no untargetability. Telling a player their 120-second ultimate cancels her 140-second one would be a very expensive thing to be wrong about, so I left it out. QUESTION FOR THE USER, not blocking: this matchup is 44.12% over 50 games yet the full layer rates it EVEN at 5.5/10 with Camille carry threat 6/10. Every stage of the prose now reads Camille-favoured through first item. If the rating should move to reflect a sub-45% win rate, diff / diffRating / carryRating and breakdown.difficulty and report[14].t all need to move together; I did not touch them because 50 games is a thin sample.
